note: Party platforms for the enrichment roadmap axis K (T: declared, coarse manifesto directions, not sourced point estimates). Each platform is a target lever bundle a government of that party would pursue through the existing bill path. Values sit inside the lever bounds in data/modern/jpn/levers.json. Parties without a platform entry (JCP, Sanseito, others) are treated as non-governing protest parties and never lead or join a government in the formation rule. coalition_order lists each potential senior partner's preferred junior partners, in order. demographic_tilts move vote shares with electorate composition: aging (change in the 65+ share, per point) favours incumbent-conservative and pensioner parties; urbanization (change in the Kanto population share, per point) favours reform and younger-voter parties. All tilts are declared (T).

CDP.stance: livelihood first: larger child benefits, lower consumption tax, cheaper healthcare, renewables over nuclear restarts

DPFP.stance: take-home pay: lower income and consumption taxes, fuel-cost relief

Ishin.stance: small government and reform: spending restraint, lower corporate tax, social-insurance reform, free education

Komeito.stance: welfare partner: child benefits, education, relief on daily-life costs

LDP.stance: security and growth: defence build-up toward 2% of GDP, industrial policy, moderate family support

Reiwa.stance: anti-austerity: abolish the consumption tax, large child benefits, higher corporate tax
